original_question: Let kappa : [-1, 1] -> R have a Gegenbauer expansion with some negative coefficients c_l only in degrees l > N for a large N. If the associated energy I_kappa has a discrete minimizer mu*, what bounds or structural information can be proved about the size of supp(mu*)?
target_in_paper: Section 4, Problem 4.1 in arXiv:2504.04845 ("Minimizers of the p-frame energy. Distances on the torus"); the immediate nearby context is Conjecture 4.1, and the motivating background comes from the companion p-frame papers cited there, especially Conjecture 1.1, Theorem 1.2, and Theorem 1.3 of ref. [3].
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper's actual target. It correctly identifies the kernel setting on [-1,1], the role of negative Gegenbauer coefficients appearing only at high degrees, the conditional assumption that a discrete minimizer exists, and the fact that the question is specifically about how large the support of such a minimizer must be.
missing_details: The ambient space is the real sphere S^{d-1} with d >= 2; this is implicit from the start of Section 4.
The energy functional should be stated explicitly as I_kappa(mu) = ∬_{S^{d-1} x S^{d-1}} kappa(<x,y>) dmu(x) dmu(y), minimized over Borel probability measures mu on S^{d-1}.
The relevant Gegenbauer basis depends on d, namely C_ell^{((d-2)/2)}; the draft leaves this dimension parameter implicit.

The paper's coefficient hypothesis is existential: there exists a negative coefficient in some high degree, i.e. c_ell < 0 for some large ell > N. Your wording can be read more strongly as saying that all negative coefficients occur only in degrees > N.
The paper does not assume uniqueness of the minimizer and does not single out a distinguished minimizer mu*; it asks conditionally about any discrete minimizer.
Because the minimizer is assumed discrete, 'size of the support' should be made explicit as the cardinality, or at least the cardinality/structure, of supp(mu).

To stay paper-faithful, the question should be linked to the surrounding p-frame context: Conjecture 4.1 asks whether all non-even p-frame minimizers are discrete, while the companion results only give existence of some discrete minimizers under stronger coefficient hypotheses and empty-interior support under weaker ones.
refined_question: Let d >= 2, let kappa:[-1,1] -> R have Gegenbauer expansion kappa(t) = sum_{ell>=0} c_ell C_ell^{((d-2)/2)}(t), and consider the energy I_kappa(mu) = ∬_{S^{d-1} x S^{d-1}} kappa(<x,y>) dmu(x) dmu(y) over Borel probability measures mu on S^{d-1}. Assume that kappa has a negative Gegenbauer coefficient in some sufficiently high degree, namely c_ell < 0 for some large ell > N. If I_kappa admits a discrete minimizing measure mu, what bounds or structural restrictions can one prove for the cardinality of supp(mu)?
justification: The draft is essentially a paraphrase of Problem 4.1, so I kept the target narrow and did not replace it by the broader discreteness conjecture. I only made the question stand-alone by restoring the ambient sphere, the measure class, the definition of I_kappa, and the sphere-dependent Gegenbauer expansion. I also corrected the coefficient hypothesis to the paper's exact existential form ('there exists some large ell > N with c_ell < 0') rather than the stronger reading that all negative coefficients are confined to high degrees. The nearby context shows why this is the right sharpening: Conjecture 4.1 states the desired discreteness phenomenon for non-even p-frame energies, while the companion paper [3] gives a quantitative support bound only under the much stronger assumption that there are only finitely many positive coefficients, and proves merely empty-interior support for general non-even p-frame kernels.
